punchline: Waiting until you can do it perfectly is just a respectable way of never beginning.
thirty_sec: In The Now Habit, Neil Fiore argued that procrastination is usually fear, not laziness. When a task feels like a verdict on your worth, avoiding it feels safer, so people prepare endlessly and never start. His fix was to aim for starting instead of finishing: work for about thirty minutes, allow the first attempt to be rough, log the time you actually worked, and keep starting. Small starts add up to finished work.
question: What have you been getting ready for so long that you could simply begin it today?
